original_text: Figure 1: Using historical access pattern creates a trade-off between cache hit rate and SSD lifetime. Gandalf maintains cache hit rate while increasing SSD lifetime.
Table 1: Reuse pattern of first round’s KV caches in multi-round conversation
Table 2: Under KV cache offloading workloads, SSDs may last less than a year—far short of their five-year warranty.
Figure 2: Under same acquisition budget, SSD is more optimal to be used for KV cache offloading workload, which is reuse-heavy.
Figure 3: Existing systems trades off SSD lifetime and cache hit rate.

Figure 4: Gandalf overview. Gandalf admits new KV caches to host memory and, when it is full, chooses between dropping a DRAM cache or moving it to SSD based on SSD write and replacement-cache recomputation costs.
Figure 5: CPU/SSD capacity ratio to obtain maximum SSD lifetime improvement.
Figure 6: In Claude Code WEKA trace, most linear-attention states are reused once or never.
Table 3: The traces writes exceed the SSD’s workload DWPD rating.

Figure 7: SSD lifetime against cache miss ratio for Gandalf and the baselines on all traces with Kimi-K3 model, 100 GB of DRAM and a 1 TB SSD. Gandalf , LRU-K, HotPrefix and Marconi are lines through their hyperparameters (Gandalf ’s 𝛼, LRU-K’s 𝐾, HotPrefix’s hotness frequency, and Marconi’s 𝛼).

Figure 8: Gandalf achieves lower cache miss ratio while achieving higher SSD lifetime under different DRAM/SSD capacity ratios. We fix the total capacity of DRAM and SSD to 4TB to make sure the cache miss ratio and lifetime is comparable across different setups.
Figure 9: Gandalf improves baselines in wide range of hybrid models having different linear-to-full cache size ratios.
Figure 10: Gandalf SSD admission results in higher fraction of SSD writes that contributes to cache hits at least once. Unlike baselines, Gandalf cache hit is stable across time.
Figure 11: A bigger portion of linear state cache hit in Gandalf comes from DRAM, while most full attention KV cache hit comes from SSD.
Figure 12: The gain from Gandalf comes from both reducing the amount of writes to the SSD (left) and increasing the Read/Write ratio (right).
Figure 13: Gandalf increases SSD lifetime while maintaining low cache load latency.
Figure 14: Average cost per request, recomputation plus SSD wear, on ClaudeCode with Kimi-K3, 100 GB of DRAM and a 1 TB SSD. Gandalf has the lowest cost once the SSD wear is counted.
